subsection.p: The most common mistakes come from forgetting one of these meanings. A definite integral is signed accumulation. An indefinite integral is a family of functions. A substitution changes both the integrand and the limits. A formula for an antiderivative must be valid on the interval where it is used.

exercise.title: Why are the two parts of the Fundamental Theorem the same story?

statement.p: Part I differentiates an accumulation and recovers the integrand. Part II integrates a derivative and recovers net change. In your own words, why are these not two unrelated formulas, but the same hinge of calculus read in opposite directions?

hint.p: One direction starts with a rate and builds a running total. The other starts with a running total and reads its rate. Each undoes the other.

exercise.title: What must you carry along when you change variables or reverse direction?

statement.p: A substitution changes the integrand, and reversing an interval changes the sign. In your own words, why are orientation and the new limits part of the meaning of the integral rather than extra bookkeeping?

hint.p: The small piece being added is height times oriented step. Changing the coordinate or the direction changes that step, so the description of the accumulation must change with it.
